title: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie Settle Winery Lawsuit That Revealed Abuse Allegations
description:
Brad Pitt has settled his legal battle with ex-wife Angelina Jolie over the sale of her stake in the couple’s winery in France.

	Pitt sued Jolie i
body:
Brad Pitt has settled his legal battle with ex-wife Angelina Jolie over the sale of her stake in the couple’s winery in France.

	Pitt sued Jolie in 2022, accusing her of selling her 50% share in Château Miraval to a subsidiary of Stoli, the Russian spirits company, without Pitt’s approval. The litigation drew attention to Jolie’s allegation that Pitt abused her and the couple’s children on a private plane in 2016, precipitating the couple’s divorce.
	

	“We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further,” representatives for Jolie and Pitt said in a statement on Wednesday. “Any comments in media stories attributed to ‘sources’ are in fact not coming from either of us, or anyone close to us.”

	Terms of the agreement were not disclosed. Pitt has also sued Yuri Shefler, the Russian-born billionaire who owns the Stoli Group. That portion of the litigation is ongoing.

	Pitt and Jolie bought the Miraval estate in 2008, and were married there in 2014. They invested tens of millions of dollars in the 1,300-acre property in order to turn Château Miraval into a profitable rosé brand.

	Jolie filed for divorce in 2016, and the fate of the winery has been in dispute ever since. Pitt has argued that the company was his “passion,” that he poured his energies into making it a success, and that Jolie has forced him into an unworkable arrangement with Stoli, a competitor. In a cross-complaint filed in 2022, Jolie accused Pitt attempting to seize control from her and of “looting” it for other ventures.

	“Pitt is an actor, not a winemaker. He deals in illusions, not dirt and grapes,” Jolie’s lawyers wrote. “While he no doubt visited the vineyards to admire the work of the French laborers who actually made the business successful, Pitt is no vigneron.”
	

	According to her cross-complaint, Jolie initially planned to sell her half of the winery to Pitt. But in 2021, the deal fell apart. According to her, Pitt conditioned the buyout on her willingness to sign a non-disclosure agreement about the domestic abuse incident that led to their divorce.

	The cross-complaint alleged that during a flight from France to the U.S., Pitt drunkenly grabbed her by the head and pushed her into a wall of the plane. The suit also claimed that Pitt lunged at one of the couple’s children, poured beer on Jolie and the children as they tried to sleep, and then refused to let the family leave the plane for 20 minutes after it landed.

	Her complaint alleged that Pitt “sought to use Château Miraval as leverage to coerce Jolie into keeping quiet about Pitt’s behavior. This new demand essentially imposed a poison pill, all but ensuring that no deal could ever be reached.”

	Rather than accept that condition, Jolie sold her stake to Stoli. She alleged that the couple had no agreement not to sell to a third party.

	A judge denied Jolie’s demurrer in November 2024, finding that Pitt’s claims were adequately pled.

	The parties have since been engaged in disputes over access to financial records and over jurisdictional issues. Pitt has accused Stoli and Shefler of attempting a “hostile takeover” of the wine business. In June, an appellate court revived Pitt’s case against them, finding that Shefler, a Swiss resident, can be sued in California.

schema.headline: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie Settle Winery Lawsuit That Revealed Abuse Allegations

title: NBC Plans to Give Thanksgiving Parade Ads Extra Run After Macy’s Postponement
description:
NBC has a Thanksgiving Week present for advertisers scheduled to appear in the now-postponed Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade.

	The network plans to
body:
NBC has a Thanksgiving Week present for advertisers scheduled to appear in the now-postponed Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade.

	The network plans to run commercials from sponsors of the event twice this week — once when the 2026 parade airs on Saturday and once on Thursday, when the network will run a repeat of last year’s Macy’s extravaganza. In short, Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade advertisers get two runs on the network for ther price of one. The details were confirmed by an NBC spokesperson.
	

	Macy’s and NBC decided to postpone the parade to Saturday, November 28, citing extreme wind conditions and inclement weather expected on Thursday. Many of the signature balloons used in the parade cannot be controlled properly during high wind speeds. The network said it is “committed to ensuring this remains a high-priority opportunity for our clients with both the reach and scale of tomorrow’s re-airing and the original live telecast on Saturday.”

	NBC has many reasons to keep advertisers in the parade happy. The cost of a 30-second commercial in the parade is up 15% to 20% over last year, according to Guideline, a tracker of ad spending, when NBC was able to charge between $900,000 and $1 million per unit. Those figures would indicate that a 30-second spot in the 2026 parade could cost between$1.03 million and $1.2 million. Ad spend on the event is pacing about 25% to 30% ahead of last year, according to Guideline. The parade snared more than $88.7 million in ads last year, the company says.

	The parade is also part of a time-honored lineup that includes the National Dog Show and a primetime NFL game. The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade telecast was the opening event in a extended schedule of holiday programs that the network uses to lure marketers eager to court holiday shoppers.
	

	Geico had plans to run a two-minute commercial that uses stop-motion animation featuring many of its  trademark characters, such as the Geico Gecko. Starbucks had signed on to promote a new holiday album, “The Holiday Blend,” and is the sponsor of a takeover of an NBC livestream of the parade on TikTok.  

	NBC isn’t the first TV network to confront delays tied to a massive live event. CBS in 2013 gave some of the advertisers in that year’s Super Bowl an extra run of their commercials after a 35-minute power outage brought a game between the Baltimore Ravens and the San Francisco 49’ers. Bud Light and Subway were among the marketers that enjoyed an extra airing of ads that had multi-million-dollar price tags.

schema.headline: NBC Plans to Give Thanksgiving Parade Ads Extra Run After Macy’s Postponement

title: King Crimson Original Drummer Michael Giles Dies at 84
description: Michael Giles, whose drumming on King Crimson’s legendary debut album brought fire and abandon to an already wild and innovative sound, has died, a
body:
Michael Giles, whose drumming on King Crimson’s legendary debut album brought fire and abandon to an already wild and innovative sound, has died, according to a post on the band’s website. No cause of death was announced; he was 84.

	“His extraordinary rhythmic imagination, musical sensitivity and highly inventive approach to drumming were fundamental to the band’s pioneering sound,” the announcement reads in part. “Michael’s originality, musical curiosity and uncompromising commitment to creative freedom challenged conventions and inspired generations of musicians around the world. He leaves behind an extraordinary musical legacy, and his unique contribution to the evolution of progressive music will never be forgotten.”
	

	Born in 1942, Giles — pictured above, bottom right, with Crimson in 1969 — hailed from Bournemouth on England’s south coast, along with Crimson cofounders Robert Fripp (far left) and Greg Lake (top). In 1967, he formed a group with his brother Peter and Fripp called, naturally enough, Giles, Giles and Fripp. The trio released an album titled “The Cheerful Insanity of Giles, Giles and Fripp” the following year, to extremely modest commercial results. However, the album laid the groundwork for King Crimson, which Giles formed late in 1968 with Fripp, vocalist/ bassist Lake, multi-instrumentalist Ian McDonald and lyricist Peter Sinfield.

	Crimson’s early concerts electrified the British rock scene, to the extend that the band was invited to open for the Rolling Stones at its massive concert in London’s Hyde Park in July of 1969. The group’s innovative sound, as captured on its debut album, “In the Court of the Crimson King,” combined rock, jazz, classical and avant-garde music into a concoction that many consider to be the first true progressive-rock album; certainly nothing like it had been heard during the rock era. (A telling example can be found in this December 1969 live recording of the album’s title track, in which Fripp gives a four-count and an eruption of sound ensues.)
	

	Its influence was profound, and can be heard everywhere from the music of fellow prog-rock travelers Yes and Genesis as well as David Bowie, Roxy Music and countless later acolytes like Tool and the Mars Volta; its song “20 th Century Schizoid Man” was famously sampled by Kanye West on his 2010 single “Power.”

	Giles’ wild drumming was key to the band’s first lineup, embellishing its classical-tinged sound with innovative, thunderous drum rolls and lightning-fast rhythms.

	However, in a trend that would follow throughout Crimson’s long existence, this lineup was short-lived: By early 1970, McDonald, Lake and Giles had all left the band, although the latter two did contribute to the band’s second album, “In the Wake of Poseidon.”

	Giles subsequently recorded an album with McDonald under the name McDonald and Giles (naturally enough), and over the years performed on recordings with an unusually diverse array of artists, including erstwhile bandmates Lake and Sinfield as well as Steve Winwood, Bryan Ferry, Leo Sayer, original Genesis guitarist Anthony Phillips, Kevin Ayers, Neil Sedaka, Yvonne Elliman, Andy Summers and the Penguin Cafe Orchestra.

	He also released a solo album titled “Progress, Ghost Dance” with later Crimson member Jamie Muir and David Cunningham, and the Michael Giles MAD Band, which featured yet another Crimson alumnus, Keith Tippett.

	He and several other alums united in 2002 to form the 21st Century Schizoid Band, which toured performing the band’s early repertoire.

	He is survived by his five children, Tina, Amanda, William, Rosie and Oliver, several grandchildren, his sister Marion and brother Peter.

schema.headline: King Crimson Original Drummer Michael Giles Dies at 84

title: ‘The Hawk’ Starring Will Ferrell Canceled After One Season at Netflix
description:
“The Hawk” has hit the rough. Netflix has canceled the golf comedy series after just one season. 

	The series, which starred Will Ferrell in his f
body:
“The Hawk” has hit the rough. Netflix has canceled the golf comedy series after just one season. 

	The series, which starred Will Ferrell in his first regular TV role since “SNL,” originally debuted on the streamer back in July. While the show did make it into the Netflix global top 10 chart for three weeks upon its release, the cost of the series, which sources say was increased by Ferrell’s salary as star and co-creator, raised the bar for success that would have led to a second season. 
	

	The official logline for “The Hawk” states “Lonnie Hawkins (Ferrell) ,2004’s number one golfer, struggles on the back nine of his career to recapture his magic. His body says retire, but his heart says he’s not done yet. His ex-wife and his son Lance, golf’s new golden boy, know he’s through. But with one more major to win to complete golf’s Grand Slam, Lonnie refuses to believe he’s anything other than one stroke away from the greatest comeback in golf history.”

	Along with Ferrell, the cast included Molly Shannon, Jimmy Tatro, Fortune Feimster, Luke Wilson, Chris Parnell, Katelyn Tarver and David Hornsby.

	Ferrell co-created the series with Harper Steele and Chris Hency. All three were executive producers along with Jessica Elbaum and Alix Taylor for Ferrell’s Gloria Sanchez Productions; Rian Johnson, Ram Bergman and Nena Rodrigue for T-Street; David Gordon Green; and Andrew Guest.

	While this was Ferrell’s first starring role in a Netflix show, he has produced a number of series at the streamer over the past several years and has multiple projects in the pipeline. He is executive producing new series “All the Rage,” “Prep,” and Nikki Glaser’s first scripted series as part of her Netflix Is a Joke Studios deal, all via Gloria Sanchez Productions. 
	

	Deadline first reported the cancellation news.

schema.headline: ‘The Hawk’ Starring Will Ferrell Canceled After One Season at Netflix

title: Tony Romo, After Parting Ways With CBS Sports, Named ‘Chief Predictions Officer’ of Jake Paul’s Betr Betting App
description: Former NFL quarterback and football analyst Tony Romo has landed his next gig: He’s joined Betr, the sports gambling app co-founded by Jake Paul, a
body:
Former NFL quarterback and football analyst Tony Romo has landed his next gig: He’s joined Betr, the sports gambling app co-founded by Jake Paul, as its first-ever “chief predictions officer.” 

	In the new role, Romo will serve as “a prominent face of the Betr brand,” appearing in original content, delivering sports predictions and engaging with fans across the company’s gaming products, including Picks, Predictions, Social Sportsbook, Social Casino, Arcade and Rips. As part of the agreement, Romo will become an equity stakeholder in Betr.
	

	Romo, former QB for the Dallas Cowboys, had been an on-air analyst with CBS Sports since 2017. Last month, the network announced it was parting ways with Romo. That came after Romo had pleaded no contest to a charge of operating while intoxicated stemming from an incident that took place in Milwaukee in July.

	Romo said: “I’ve spent my entire career trying to anticipate what’s going to happen next, whether that was on the field or in the broadcast booth. Now I get to put those instincts to work in a completely new way with Betr.” He added, “I’m looking forward to having some fun, making predictions and being part of where this company is headed. And I’ve got a pretty good feeling about what’s coming next.”

	“Tony Romo has built an extraordinary reputation around something that sits at the very heart of our business: predictions,” Joey Levy, founder and CEO of Betr, said in a statement. “His ability to see what’s coming before anyone else has made him one of the most compelling personalities in sports, and we see a tremendous opportunity to bring that talent and personality to our growing ecosystem.”
	

	Romo joins Betr’s roster of sports and entertainment talent partners, including NBA veteran Patrick Beverley, former Heisman Trophy winner Johnny Manziel and actors Jeremy Piven and Adrian Grenier.

schema.headline: Tony Romo, After Parting Ways With CBS Sports, Named ‘Chief Predictions Officer’ of Jake Paul’s Betr Betting App

title: ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Season 35 Finale Attracts 9.2 Million Viewers
description: “Dancing With the Stars” aired its Season 35 finale live coast-to-coast for the first time on Tuesday, and the results were big. A season-best 9.2
body:
“Dancing With the Stars” aired its Season 35 finale live coast-to-coast for the first time on Tuesday, and the results were big. A season-best 9.2 million total viewers watched Paralympic track and field athlete Ezra Frech and partner Daniella Karagach take home the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy, according to Nielsen live+same-day preliminary, panel-only program ratings. 

	According to ABC, the finale posted a 2.38 rating with adults 18-49, which made it the best number in the demo since Nov. 25, 2014 (coincidentally, the season when now-host Alfonso Ribeiro won the trophy with partner Witney Carson). The finale was also up 11% in the demo vs. last year’s telecast (2.15 rating).
	

	That 2.38 rating makes it TV’s top entertainment telecast with adults 18-49 since the Oscars in March and the highest-rated regularly scheduled entertainment telecast in 18-49 since the April 1, 2020, episode of Fox’s “The Masked Singer.”

	In total viewers, the 9.2 million viewers matched last year’s finale.

	In other demos, the finale averaged a 2.86 rating with adults 18-34 — the best performance since the Season 12 finale on May 24, 2011. With women 18-34, “Dancing With the Stars” posted a 4.46 rating, which is the best series telecast number in the demo for any network broadcast since the Season 3 premiere of Fox’s “Empire” on Sept. 21, 2016. And the show posted the best teens 12-17 rating (1.18) since “The Masked Singer” on Feb. 27, 2019.

	ABC said the finale attracted more than 86 million votes, a new high (up 19% from 72 million in 2025) — the most ever for a single episode. The finale was the No. 1 most social program on television across broadcast and cable on the night and the No. 1 most social episode of any broadcast primetime series, year-to-date.
	

	“Dancing with the Stars” aired live in every U.S. time zone for its special three-hour finale on Tuesday; the finale also re-aired in primetime in the Pacific time zone and started streaming the next day on Hulu. 

	The five final couples also included Amber Glenn and partner Pasha Pashkov, Maura Higgins and partner Mark Ballas, Connor Wood and partner Rylee Arnold and Tatyana Ali and partner Jan Ravnik.

	The three-hour event included an instant dance challenge, where the couples were tested on their ability to improvise; a “judge’s choice” round and a freestyle round. The finale kicked off with an opening number to “One More Time” by Daft Punk. The “Dancing with the Stars: Live!” 2027 tour pros performed a routine to “It’s Not Right but It’s OK (Thunderpuss Mix)” by Whitney Houston, and then all Season 35 couples returned for multiple performances. Season 34 champs Robert Irwin and Witney Carson danced to “Free Bird” by Lynyrd Skynyrd. 

	“Dancing with the Stars” is co-hosted by Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough. Ballroom judges are Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough. BBC Studios produces.

	“Dancing With the Stars” Season 35 had been building to its finale with some of its strongest ratings in years. For its penultimate episode on Nov. 17, the show hit season highs with 7.64 million total viewers and a 1.68 rating in adults 18-49, based on preliminary Live + Same Day Panel Only data. It was the best ratings for a semifinal telecast in nine years, since Season 25 on Nov. 20, 2017 and Season 24 on May 22, 2017. 

	Season to date, “Dancing With the Stars” is primetime’s No. 1 entertainment series in adults 18-49 (1.59 rating in live+same day) for the third year in a row. It’s 86% above the No. 2 show, CBS’ “Survivor” (0.86), which ABC said is the largest advantage in Nielsen electronic measurement history.

schema.headline: ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Season 35 Finale Attracts 9.2 Million Viewers

title: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed to Saturday Due to Storm
description:
Thanksgiving morning will not feature the Macy’s Parade this year due to extreme weather in New York.

	“The safety of our participants and spectat
body:
Thanksgiving morning will not feature the Macy’s Parade this year due to extreme weather in New York.

	“The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration. Due to the expected severe weather, the 100th March of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will move to Saturday, Nov. 28,” Macy’s said in a statement to NBC News on Monday. “Our team is working through the operational logistics for this change and will share details as they are finalized. We expect the Parade to kick off at 8:30a.m. on Saturday. Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year. We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.”
	

	On Thanksgiving Day, NBC will instead telecast the 2025 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones.

	Ahead of the announcement, organizers behind the parade had been monitoring the weather situation all week, worrying that strong winds in New York City would ground the iconic balloons. Parade rules prohibit giant balloons from flying if sustained winds exceed 23 mph or if gusts are 34 mph or stronger.

	Over 100 balloons and balloon handlers were set to be on display in celebration of the parade’s 100th anniversary. Buckaroo Bob the Minion, Joe Cool, Mickey’s Sorcerer’s Apprentice and Billie Brightpaw were among the balloon characters that had to be grounded. 

	Preparations for the parade balloons take months, with a village of creatives working behind the scenes to bring everything together. As early as July, the parade’s concept artist begins working on both balloon and float designs. By September, the parade’s costume designer, Kimberly Montgomery, starts piecing together over 5,000 costumes and collaborating with partners to ensure she has the right colors for the balloon handlers and accurate designs.
	

	Float performances on the schedule include Natasha Bedingfield, McKenna Grace, Jimmy Fallon & The Roots, Queen Latifah and a tribute to Dolly Parton led by Megan Hilty.

	“Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade brings the extraordinary together: iconic entertainers and emerging talent, artistry and imagination, hometown pride, cherished traditions and the thrill of discovering something new,” said Sharon Otterman, Macy’s chief marketing officer. “For our 100th Parade, we’re creating a celebration of unprecedented scale and will deliver an unforgettable Thanksgiving for millions across the country.”

	NBC and Peacock are still set to air “Countdown to Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade” Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET.

schema.headline: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed to Saturday Due to Storm

title: Andy Taylor, Duran Duran Guitarist, Dies at 65
description: Guitarist Andy Taylor, whose tenure in England’s glammy, pop-savvy rock band Duran Duran coincided with the group’s commercial pinnacle of the earl
body:
Guitarist Andy Taylor, whose tenure in England’s glammy, pop-savvy rock band Duran Duran coincided with the group’s commercial pinnacle of the early ‘80s, died of prostate cancer at his home on Monday while surrounded by family. He was 65.

	In a statement shared with Variety, Taylor’s wife Tracey said on behalf of their family, “To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather. He was the rock of our family. For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first. Nothing made him happier than having us all together, and no matter how far music took him, his heart was always at home.”
	

	Duran Duran added, “Andy was there at the very beginning of our story. From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.”

	Taylor, who was diagnosed with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer in 2018, had opted out on appearing at the group’s November 2022 induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, citing a decline in his health in a statement.

	He said, “Although my current condition is not immediately life-threatening there is no cure…. Recently I was doing OK after some very sophisticated life-extending treatment, that was until a week or so ago when I suffered a setback, and despite the exceptional efforts of my team, I had to be honest in that both physically and mentally, I would be pushing my boundaries.”
	

	Duran Duran had been in existence for two years in the Midlands city of Birmingham when Taylor — then a 19-year-old Northumberland native seeking new opportunities after successfully touring British army bases in Europe with cover bands — spotted a April 1980 Melody Maker classified ad seeking a “Live Wire Guitarist.” 

	He wrote in “Wild Boy,” his candid and frequently sensational 2008 autobiography, “[The ad] cited Mick Ronson of the Spiders From Mars and Steve Jones of the Sex Pistols as musical influences so I thought it looked worth a call.”

	After a successful audition, Taylor became a member of the quintet, which became a popular fixture at the Birmingham club the Rum Runner. Sporting extravagant coiffs and makeup — “We’d end up discussing cosmetics with the girls,” Taylor later wrote — the band was lumped in with Britain’s New Romantic movement of the early ‘80s. After only eight months with Taylor in the lineup, the act was signed by EMI.

	Duran Duran — whose early compositions were credited to all five group members — became a nearly instant success in the U.K. Its third single “Girls on Film” (No. 5) helped push its self-titled debut album to No. 3. The 1982 follow-up album “Rio” spawned the hits “Hungry Like the Wolf” (No. 5) and the eponymous single (No. 9). Its first No. 1 single “Is There Something I Should Know” was issued in 1983.

	The band was among the first beneficiaries of Stateside exposure on MTV, the then-new cable network that broke through with wall-to-wall airing of videos; their lavish clips, handsomely directly by former 10cc members Kevin Godley and Lol Creme and the prolific Russell Mulcahy, captured eyes with their lush cinematography, scantily clad models and expensive location shoots in exotic locales like Sri Lanka and Antigua. Three Duran Duran singles reached the U.S. top five in 1982-83.

	Taylor noted in his memoir that those videos often found the band members risking life and limb: “They were enormous fun to make — even if it nearly killed us at times. I’m not joking! Several of us risked being drowned, we narrowly escaped being trampled by a crazed elephant, and we were forced to flee one shoot after being threatened by four thousand angry monks.”Unsurprisingly, Duran Duran’s only Grammy Awards, both presented in 1986, were for best short form music video and (for “Duran Duran,” a compilation of their first 12 clips) best long form music video.
	

	By 1983, the act was big enough in England to headline a London charity benefit attended by Prince Charles and Princess Diana, who told its members, “I don’t need any introductions to these boys. I know exactly who they are.” Their album of that year, “Seven and the Ragged Tiger,” shot to No. 1 in the U.K. and No. 8 in the U.S.

	However, by 1984, when the singles “The Reflex” and “The Wild Boys” reached No. 1 and No. 2 respectively in both the U.K. and the U.S. (thanks in no small part to the participation of Chic cofounder and David Bowie/ Madonna producer Nile Rodgers), the band’s hard-partying, notoriously debauched lifestyle was beginning to shred their reputation; a story in the Fleet Street tabloid the Sun detailed stories of extreme cocaine abuse — later verified by Taylor, who, with bassist John Taylor (no relation), was the drug’s most enthusiastic user. Additional turmoil came into the guitarist’s life that year after his wife Tracey suffered a postpartum psychotic episode following the birth of their son Andrew.

	Wrung out from a grueling recording and touring schedule and increasingly debilitated by their drug habits, Andy and John Taylor made a lateral move into a new quartet, the Power Station, which also featured British R&B singer Robert Palmer and Chic’s drummer Tony Thompson. Produced by Thompson’s bandmate Bernard Edwards, its self-titled 1985 debut reached No. 6 in the U.S. and No. 12 in the U.K. (A long-delayed 1996 sequel, with Edwards standing in on bass for John Taylor, then in rehab, failed to chart.)

	By the time Duran Duran appeared at the U.S. incarnation of the transatlantic, internationally televised benefit concert Live Aid in July 1985, the original lineup of the group was reaching the end of its tether. Taylor wrote in his memoir, “John and I were in a dark place….[W]e were dying inside. We were tired of twenty-four-hour attention, tired of drinking and taking drugs, haggard from the lifestyle we had once aspired to.”

	Exiting the band in 1986, Taylor attempted to clean up his life in Los Angeles and began working with Steve Jones, the former guitarist for the Sex Pistols and himself then newly in recovery. The fruits of their collaboration included “Take It Easy,” a No. 24 pop hit heard on the soundtrack for the film “American Anthem,” and the tough “I Might Lie,” which rose to No. 17 on Billboard’s mainstream rock chart. His 1987 solo set “Thunder” reached No. 46 domestically.
	

	Following occasional work behind Rod Stewart, Taylor rejoined Duran Duran, after an absence of 14 years, for a full reunion of the original band. A successful world tour and a new album, 2004’s “Astronaut” (No. 3 in the U.K., No. 17 in the U.S.), followed. But the guitarist soon became discontent again, and exited a second time in 2006; material he had worked on for a new album was shelved.

	“I was tired of going over and over the same old creative difficulties and financial tensions,” he later wrote, “and I was fed up with having blazing rows with our management over what I perceived to be our lack of clear direction….We’d ceased to function as a band; it was seriously dysfunctional. We’d returned to being five individuals pulling in different directions, just as we’d become in the eighties. When it came to sorting out our problems, just like before, we failed to connect.”

	He then entered a long hiatus from music that ended in 2019, when he toured and released a solo single. He produced a 2022 album by the band Reef, and then reunited with Duran Duran for their 2023 album, “Danse Macabre.” That Halloween-themed album, which featured the original lineup and, on one song, a reunion with Nile Rodgers, combined three new originals with covers of their own songs as well as covers of songs by artists ranging from the Rolling Stones and Billie Eilish to Siouxsie & the Banshees and the Specials. Also that year, Taylor released a final solo album, “Man’s a Wolf to Man.” 

	He is survived by wife Tracey and his children Andrew, Isabelle, Bethany and Georgina.

schema.headline: Andy Taylor, Duran Duran Guitarist, Dies at 65

title: New ‘Rocky’ Book Celebrates 50th Anniversary With Rare and Never-Seen-Before Paintings
description:
Sylvester Stallone‘s classic film “Rocky” premiered half a century ago.

	To mark the occasion, artist John Rivoli has released a new book, “The Fi
body:
Sylvester Stallone‘s classic film “Rocky” premiered half a century ago.

	To mark the occasion, artist John Rivoli has released a new book, “The Fine Art Of Rocky: An Artistic Tribute From Screen To Canvas,” published by Insight Editions.

	The book features rare and never-before-seen original Rocky paintings by Rivoli, an official MGM/Amazon Rocky artist. 


	Part art book and part analysis of the six Rocky films, the book invites fans to revisit the iconic franchise through Rivoli’s collection of large-scale original paintings and iconic posters, seeing the beloved character in a whole new light.
	

	Rocky takes center stage in this deluxe book, with over 70 of Rivoli’s paintings, posters and other unique artworks highlighting unforgettable moments from the films presented in original and unique perspectives as well as art collaborations with Stallone.


			
			
			
			
	

	
					

	Rivoli said, “This book represents a lifetime of training — for this moment, for this story, for this opportunity to reinterpret Rocky through my own artistic lens.” 

	Speaking with Variety, Rivoli pointed to two pieces featured in the book. The first, “Alone in the Ring,” is something that holds a special place in his heart. “I struggled with how to tell this story visually. I knew that to capture the true significance of the moment, I had to make Rocky small on the canvas. As an artist, that’s a difficult decision when you know collectors want a large, commanding image of Rocky hanging on their walls.”

	Rivoli says the painting wasn’t about making Rocky larger than life. “It was about showing him surrounded by something much bigger than himself. The ring is enormous, the arena is vast, and the towering image of Apollo Creed dominates the space. Everything around Rocky is larger than he is, emphasizing just how small and alone he feels in that moment.”
	

	It’s also a turning point in the film as Rocky’s goal shifts from wanting to win the fight to something far more meaningful: going the distance and proving to himself that he’s not just another bum from the neighborhood.

	“That realization is the emotional heart of the story, and it’s what I wanted the painting to communicate.”



	

	



	Another meaningful work of art is “The Chosen One.” Rivoli reveals the original hangs in Stallone’s home. He says, “It captures the very foundation of the film and the character study that Sylvester Stallone so brilliantly establishes in its opening moments. ‘Rocky’ begins with an image of Jesus. The camera slowly pans down, revealing the word ‘Resurrection,’ before ultimately introducing us to Rocky Balboa. In that beautifully constructed sequence, we’re being told something profound: we’re about to witness the resurrection or redemption of this man.” He adds, “I find that moment incredibly powerful and I wanted to capture its spiritual and emotional significance on canvas.”

	“My hope is that readers don’t just experience the film again, but feel it in a way they never have before — as if they’re seeing Rocky for the very first time. If it moves them, if it reveals something new, then I’ve done what I set out to do.”

	This richly illustrated volume reimagines Rocky as an immersive artistic celebration, bringing moments from screen to canvas, which invites fans to experience the iconic character in a bold new light across his 50-year legacy. 

	Insight Editions will release a deluxe hardcover edition with 176 pages. A signed limited edition is available at insighteditions.com, with regular editions available at amazon.com

title: ‘Steven Universe’ Star Zyri Comes Out as Trans
description: Zyri, who voiced the titular character in “Steven Universe” and played Brian Corbett on “The Goldbergs,” has come out as trans. In a Substack post
body:
Zyri, who voiced the titular character in “Steven Universe” and played Brian Corbett on “The Goldbergs,” has come out as trans. In a Substack post on Wednesday, Zyri wrote about the challenges of being a child star and coming to terms with their gender identity.

	“Coming to terms with my dysphoria and my transness was only a small piece of my journey towards being a whole, authentic person, but it was notable as the first thing that truly felt like mine in my entire life,” Zyri wrote. “That’s also why for a time I was so terrified of being outed: I didn’t want to lose my newfound light the way I’d lost control of my name, my childhood, and my entire identity to the brand I was molded into by others. I know now that I really had nothing to fear there — the only thing that defines me is me — but I’ve had to continuously unlearn being afraid of losing all of myself again. That’s probably something I’ll have to remind myself of for the rest of my life, but at least now, for the very first time, I can envision the rest of my life. I celebrated my twenty-eighth birthday just over a year ago now, and the symbolic nature of that number shouldn’t be lost on anyone who grew up like I did. What twenty-one year old me would’ve cynically viewed as being past my cosmically-assigned expiration date, is now something that truly feels worth celebrating. To any of you poor souls who had to suffer my angst-riddled but still disconcertingly genuine former aspirations to wrap my life up at twenty-seven, I’m terribly sorry, and am also happy to report that I didn’t even come close to sticking the landing.”
	


	Zyri voiced Steven Universe and several other characters on the Cartoon Network series across all five seasons and 160 episodes, in addition to a TV movie, a follow-up series and several video games. Zyri’s TV debut came in 2009 on “Are You Smarter Than a Fifth Grader?,” and they also appeared in episodes of “Hannah Montana,” “iCarly,” “Fresh Off the Boat,” “Henry Danger” and animated titles like “The Legend of Korra,” “Justice League: War,” “Batman: The Long Halloween, Part Two,” “Injustice” and many more. Zyri also gave an update that they have been married for a year and will “wade back into” performing after not appearing in a live-action project since 2019 and an animated role since 2024.
	

	“As for the future, my hope is that not too much changes in my daily life going forward,” Zyri wrote. “I do genuinely love and miss performing and creating, though it’s only very recently that I’ve felt well enough to wade back into it. I recognize that my job often requires some degree of public visibility, but for the foreseeable future I intend to only engage in that when it’s necessary, rather than proactively. I do place an extremely high value on privacy these days, and while there will always be some blurring of the lines between personal and professional life, I’m very happy to have actually separated the two for the first time and I don’t wish to give that up again. Being a child performer has a way of capturing your psychological development and splicing those two pieces together until they’re simply the same thing; everything I’ve written about overcoming here could be summed up as the process of carefully untangling them from each other until they’re the way they ought to be.”

body:
Duran Duran Icon
                          Andy Taylor Dead at 65
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 25, 2026
                            1:54 PM PST
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  November 25, 2026
                                2:52 PM PST
                                    
      
    
              Andy Taylor, the iconic guitarist behind some of Duran Duran's biggest hits, has died following a years-long battle with prostate cancer.
      
    
              The musician died Monday at age 65 after battling stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer, which he was diagnosed with in 2018.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Taylor’s wife, Tracey, confirmed his death Wednesday in a heartfelt family statement, remembering him as a devoted husband, father and grandfather ... while his Duran Duran bandmates paid tribute to the guitarist who helped shape their sound and success.
      

              Taylor helped shape Duran Duran's signature sound throughout the 1980s ... contributing to massive hits like "Hungry Like the Wolf," "Rio" and "The Reflex." He was also a member of the supergroup The Power Station and worked with artists including Robert Palmer and Rod Stewart.
      
    
              In 2022, Taylor's bandmates revealed his cancer diagnosis during Duran Duran's induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ... reading a letter from the guitarist explaining why his declining health prevented him from attending the ceremony.
      
    
              Despite his diagnosis, Taylor continued making music while undergoing treatment ... releasing his solo album "Man's a Wolf to Man" in 2023.
      
    
              He was 65.
      
    
              RIP

              Mother Nature is crashing Thanksgiving ... the iconic Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed as a nasty storm threatens to wreak havoc on New York City.
      
    
              Macy's announced Wednesday the annual spectacle is being pushed from Thanksgiving morning to Saturday ... with powerful winds and heavy rain raising serious safety concerns for spectators and participants.
      
    
              The decision comes as the parade celebrates its 100th edition ... with the massive character balloons particularly vulnerable to dangerous wind gusts.
      
    
              And for anyone planning to watch from the couch Thursday ... NBC will air a rerun of last year's parade instead.
      
    
              Looks like Santa's coming to town a couple days late this year.
